---
title: "Course preparations"
---

In order to have a smooth workshop start, you need to prepare a few technical things
so you can jump right into using Git on the first day.

# Install Git on your machine

You can follow my guide below but you can also find the download and installation guides for all major operating systems
[on the official Git website](https://git-scm.com/downloads).
If you have an old version of Git already installed, please make sure to update it
prior to the workshop. You can checkout [this article](https://www.howtogeek.com/759319/how-to-check-and-update-your-git-version/)
that explains how to find your current Git version and how to update to a newer one.

:::{.panel-tabset}

# Windows

You can download Git from [here](https://git-scm.com/download/win).

Download and install the correct version for your machine (just click "Click here to download"). Use recommended or default settings during the installation. Most options can also be changed later if you want to.

With the Git installation for Windows, you also get a program called "Git Bash". 
Git Bash is a terminal application for Windows that provides a Git command line experience.

Open the Git Bash application (you can find it searching in the Windows search bar) 
and run (just type it and hit Enter)

```sh
git --version
```

If the Git installation was successful, you should see the version of Git printed to the console.

# Linux (Ubuntu)

You can install Git from the terminal. Run

```sh
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install git
```

Check the version of Git that you have installed with

```sh
git --version
```

# macOS

Open the Terminal app and run

```sh
git --version
```

If Git is already installed, you will see the version of Git printed to the console.

If Git is not installed yet, macOS will ask you to install the "command line developer tools". Click **Install**, wait until the installation is finished and run `git --version` again to check that it worked.

Alternatively, if you use [Homebrew](https://brew.sh/), you can install Git with

```sh
brew install git
```

:::

# Sign up for GitHub

I will use GitHub as a remote repository service in the workshop and you can [create an account here](https://github.com/join). 

::: {.callout-tip}

## Free benefits for students and academic staff

Students and academic staff can get free benefits through [GitHub Education](https://github.com/education) (e.g. GitHub Pro for students, free GitHub Copilot).
These are not added automatically: you need to apply and verify your affiliation, e.g. with your institutional email address and a student ID or enrollment certificate (i.e. "Immatrikulationsbescheinigung").
You don't need any of this for the workshop but it might be interesting if you use GitHub long-term.

If you plan to apply, adding your institutional email address to your account helps. You can always add a second email address later or change it if you leave your institution.

:::

# Install GitHub Desktop

In the course, I'll be using the GitHub Desktop application as a graphical user
interface to work with Git.

There are detailed step by step guides on how to install and set up GitHub Desktop
on the GitHub Website. Please follow [this guide](https://docs.github.com/en/desktop/installing-and-configuring-github-desktop/installing-and-authenticating-to-github-desktop/setting-up-github-desktop#part-1-installing-github-desktop) and 
do Part 1 (Installing GitHub Desktop) and Part 2 (Configuring your account).

When GitHub Desktop asks you to **configure Git**, enter your name and the email address of your GitHub account. This information is shown on all your commits.
You can check or change it later under **File -> Options -> Git** (macOS: **GitHub Desktop -> Settings -> Git**).
This setting is also used when you work with Git in the terminal, RStudio or VS Code.

:::{.callout-note}

## Linux users

If you are running a Linux OS, you can install GitHub Desktop from the [shiftkey repository](https://github.com/shiftkey/desktop) as
on the GitHub Desktop website, there is only a Windows and MacOS version available.
When you are done with the installation step, please head over to the GitHub Desktop documentation linked
above and follow Part 2 (Configuring your account).

:::
